title: Functorial acyclic finite-prefix resolution of an abelian tower
statement: Let T be the abelian category of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by natural numbers [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-pc-tower-abelian], with enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives], and let L=lim be additive with right derived functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let P:T -> Ab send A to product_n A_n with componentwise maps, and let t:P -> P be 1 minus shift [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. There exist functors U,V:T -> T, natural maps i:Id -> U and p:U -> V with pi=0 and 0 -> A -> U(A) -> V(A) -> 0 short exact for every A, natural isomorphisms e_U:L U -> P and e_V:L V -> P with L(p_A) e_V(A)=e_U(A)t_A, and R^q L(U(A))=R^q L(V(A))=0 for every A and q>=1.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1, proof: finite-prefix systems B and C

proof.text: For a tower A indexed by n >= 0, define U(A)_n as the finite product of A_i with i <= n and V(A)_n as the finite product with i < n. Both transitions forget the last coordinate. Define i_A at n by all composites of transitions from A_n to A_i. Define p_A at n by x_i - f_i(x_(i+1)) for i < n. Coordinatewise maps induced by a morphism of towers commute with i_A,p_A and transitions, yielding functors U,V and natural transformations i,p with i_A p_A=0.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1, proof: finite-prefix systems B and C

proof.text: At level n, i_A is injective because its coordinate n is the identity. The kernel of p_A consists precisely of successive-transition tuples and is the image of i_A. Given y_i for i<n, start with x_n=0 and solve x_i=y_i+f_i(x_(i+1)) downwards, so p_A is surjective. These levelwise short exact sequences are short exact in the functor category, since its kernels and cokernels are computed levelwise by their universal properties. The empty prefix V(A)_0 is the zero group.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1, proof: finite-prefix systems B and C

proof.text: A compatible family of finite prefixes is determined uniquely by one entry in each A_i; conversely a full tuple restricts to such a family. This gives natural isomorphisms lim U(A) and lim V(A) with product_i A_i. Computing every coordinate identifies lim p_A with 1 minus the shift, namely x_i-f_i(x_(i+1)). Thus the isomorphisms intertwine lim p with the natural transition endomorphism of the product functor.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1, proof: finite-prefix systems B and C

proof.text: Both U(A) and V(A) have surjective projection transitions (extend a prefix by zero). Apply the acyclicity theorem for surjective towers to each: all positive right derived limits of U(A) and V(A) vanish.
